recap.workouts:
Three for three on a day that was supposed to be easy, and all three stayed easy. CrossFit: hang power snatch built to 110 lb, then Brown at [FITNESS] — 1h28 on the clock, avg HR 111, max 149, RPE 4. Capped and cruised, exactly the deload call. Lifting (upper push + triceps): incline DB press 65x10/9, chest fly 40x13, lateral raise 20x16/18, triceps pushdown 150x12 — every load exactly at the prescribed deload dose, nothing crept up.

CF9 — 60'14 on the trainer, 30.3 km, load 47 against a planned 51 (92.2% compliance, paired cleanly to the planned session). Your note: set the erg to the lowest number of Z2 with the new zones. That is exactly what the file shows. Warm-up 5' at 130 W, HR 117. Then the 50' block ERG-locked at 164.5 W — the floor of the new 165-196 W band — cadence 90 the whole way, then 5' down at 125 W.

The HR curve is about as boring as a Z2 curve can be, which is precisely the point. You settled at 133 bpm inside the first two minutes. Five-minute reads across the block: 131 · 133 · 134 · 133 · 134 · 133 · 132 · 133 · 134 · 134. Settled start (min 7-12) 132.9 -> final five minutes of the block 133.8, so drift was +0.9 bpm across 43 minutes. Decoupling 0.0% — watts per beat identical in both halves. Max HR for the whole hour was 143, sixteen beats under the new bike LTHR of 159, and the block sat at 84% of it. For context: the last time you rode around 164 W (19 Jul) the hour averaged 128 bpm versus 131 today — three beats up at the same output, the day after a threshold tune with Form at -20. That is residual, not a warning sign.
recap.takeaways:
1) The endurance verdict: CF9 was a genuine easy ride, and that is the whole win. Fifty minutes locked at 164.5 W, HR flat at 133 start to finish (+0.9 bpm drift), decoupling 0.0%, max 143 against LTHR 159. Essentially zero aerobic cost on the eve of the week's biggest deliverable — the ride that was labelled first-to-cut earned its place by costing you nothing.

2) You took the FLOOR of the new Z2 band, not the ceiling. Worth naming, because it is the mature call: an FTP bump rescales the numbers, it is not permission to ride harder on easy days. Same discipline in the gym — pushdown 150x12 topped its range and stays at 150 this week (banked for Week 9, per the deload rule).

3) ADAPT: no-op. CF9 EXECUTED (92.2% compliance, paired), class cruised at RPE 4 with avg HR 111, hypertrophy exact at the deload dose. Nothing in the remaining week changes. No tune analysis today — CF9 is not a tune workout, so yesterday's CT31 anchors (FTP 236 W, bike LTHR 159) stand untouched.

4) Everything now points at tomorrow. RT19 re-anchors your run zones for the entire next block. Protect it at 06:00 — Rainbow is the biggest collision on this week's calendar.
